themes.name: Getting creators to know each other
themes.note: The whole product rests on this. Forty-five people who have never spoken are a mailing list, not a community.
ideas: An opt-in that DMs two creators who have not spoken, with one shared thing to talk about: same market, same platform, overlapping travel. Runs every Monday.
A question with a title, tags and answers, separate from chat. Chat answers are lost in a week; this is searchable forever and is what somebody planning a trip actually wants.
"Answered 14 questions", visible, so being generous is a status you can see.
Automatic: lived there, or two or more answered questions about it. Surfaces on the country panel the maps now open.
Three faces on the home page, chosen by shared destination, overlapping trip dates or the same platform, with the reason written on the card. Not "suggested": explained.
A button on a profile that opens a group DM with both and a one-line reason. Warm intros beat cold ones every time.
Voice notes in DMs and rooms
Sixty seconds, waveform, no transcription. The fastest way to sound like a person instead of a username.
A message with twelve replies currently swamps a room. Threads keep the main room readable.
The rooms know what you have read and never say so. A catch-up jump to the first unread.
@everyone notifies the whole network. A room-scoped @here would get used ten times as often and annoy nobody.
"3:41pm for them" next to the DM button. Stops half the messages that never get answered.
The directory filters on language but never says "you both speak Portuguese" where it would matter.
A creator marks two hours a week as open for questions; it appears on their profile and the calendar.
A creator who leaves keeps a read-only profile and their entries. People come back, and deleting them says they were staff.
Icebreaker prompts in a quiet room
When a room has been silent for a week, the app offers the team one question worth asking, drawn from what is actually happening that month.
"Three of your connections know Ilaria." The single strongest reason anybody accepts a request from a stranger.
Not markets: hiking, food, van life, editing. Cuts across countries, which is the point.
A directory of who will answer
Opt in to being asked about a topic. The difference between a directory of people and a directory of help.

themes.name: The maps, now that countries open
themes.note: Tapping a country answers a question. These are the next questions it could answer.
ideas: A real page per country: who lives there, who has been, the questions asked about it, the videos filmed there, the deals. The panel is the teaser; this is the destination.
"I am going here" from the panel
One tap from "nobody has been to Sudan yet" to a collab-board trip.
Heat by content, not by people
Tint a country by how many challenge entries were filmed there. A different and more useful map.
Trip overlap alerts on the map
Two planes converging on the same country in the same fortnight should say so, not just both be drawn.
Filter the map by language or market
The directory filters the grid; the map ignores them.
Draw the route, not just the arc
A trip with three stops is three hops. The collab board already stores them.
A creator's own map animating their year, as a shareable video. The most shareable thing this platform could make.
The twenty countries with no creator, as an invitation. Turns a gap into a challenge.
The TopoJSON is a megabyte from a CDN. Put it in the service worker; the map is the slowest thing on the hub.
Lisbon has more in common with Lisbon than Portugal does with itself. Needs country pages first.
Visa and entry notes per country
Community-maintained, dated, with who last checked. The single most-asked question before a trip.
Crowdsourced from creators who went, not from a travel blog. Range, not average.

themes.name: Challenges, which is where the money is
ideas: Paste a link, come back later. Right now a submission is all-or-nothing at the moment of pasting.
One line from the team on every entry that did not win. The cheapest retention lever there is.
Creators critiquing each other's videos, opt in per challenge.
A brief that is a checklist
"Show the deal screen", "say the name", "under 30 seconds", ticked as you submit. Fewer disqualifications, less admin.
Two creators, one entry, prize split automatically. Forces collaboration, which forces connection.
With a weekly micro-brief inside it, so there is always something live.
Where each platform's terms allow it, so the leaderboard is not a self-reported number.
Three sentences on every results page. Teaches the standard better than any brief.
A small prize drawn from everyone who entered but did not place. Keeps the quiet majority entering.
So a new brief is a fill-in rather than a blank page.
Show the creator exactly what the card will look like on the leaderboard before they submit.
The deadline is local midnight; the reminder should be local evening, not 4am.
Funded by that market's performance, so a Romanian creator is not competing against the UK's budget.
On tryp.com, indexed, with creator credit and a link out. Free distribution for them, free SEO for us.
One place per challenge for "does a story count", answered once, visible to everyone.
Enter three in a row and it is worth saying so. Consistency is what actually compounds.

themes.name: Making a creator's work visible
ideas: One PDF: reach, best entries, countries, languages, testimonials. Creators ask brands for this constantly.
At a real URL, opt-in, indexable.
Let a creator pin three entries as their best work rather than the platform deciding by views.
What their following did over their time in the programme. The strongest recruitment asset we could have.
A personal, shareable recap in December.
As an image sized for a story.
Surfaces a creator to brands browsing the directory. Needs a brand-side view.
So briefing a paid piece stops being a negotiation from zero.
What they plan to post and when, visible to the team, so campaigns can be timed around it.
Two creators agree to feature each other; the platform tracks it and reports the lift.
Drawn from real entries that did well here, not from generic advice.

themes.name: Learning and getting better
ideas: "Your first travel video", six resources in order, with progress. Resources today are a flat list.
The team picks one entry and explains its first three seconds. Ships as a room post and a library entry.
"Look at this before I post it", 24-hour window, two reviewers.
Gear and app list per creator
Because "what do you edit on" is asked weekly.
A monthly call with somebody outside the programme, recorded into the library.
Disclosure and ad-labelling law changes by market and nobody currently tracks it.
The single most common way an entry becomes unusable.
What a three-second view actually counts as on each platform.
From past sessions. Needs the questions board.
Give it a destination and a deal, get twelve shots worth filming. Built from what has already won.
LUTs and templates the team actually uses, so a new creator's first video looks like it belongs.

themes.name: Rhythm: reasons to open the app on a Tuesday
ideas: Monday plans, Wednesday wins, Friday questions. Automated, one room post.
Streaks for posting, not just games
The games have streak freezes; the community does not.
Birthdays already exist. "One year in the programme" does not.
What happened, what is live, who joined. The email tooling exists; the digest does not.
Push for the things that matter
Challenge closing, DM, invite, and nothing else. Prefs exist; the taxonomy is too coarse.
On the home page: who is online, what was just posted.
A market proposes one, people RSVP, it lands on the calendar. The Meetups rooms are empty because there is no object to put in them.
Surface a quiet room to the whole network once a week.
Forty-eight-hour mini-challenges, no prize, just a leaderboard. Cheap and habit-forming.
Say hello exists as a full game now. Make it the third daily.
The whole app dressed for a month-long theme. Christmas markets, shoulder season, summer.

themes.name: Trust, safety and moderation
ideas: There is delete and mute for admins and nothing at all for creators.
DMs are open by request; blocking is not possible.
For reported content, with an audit trail.
The admin surface can move money now.
Anonymised. Trust is built by showing the work.
"Sign out everywhere" exists; seeing WHERE you are signed in does not.

themes.name: Money, and making it obvious
ideas: Everything earned, paid, pending, in one place. The invoice queue is admin-side only.
Approved, sent, paid. Currently silence between the two ends.
Show a Romanian creator their prize in lei with the rate and the date used.
Paid at the counted stage rather than by hand.
Consistent entrants earn a higher baseline. Rewards effort, not luck.
With real attribution, so posting a Tryp deal earns. Probably the biggest commercial idea here.
For a briefed shoot, into the same invoice pipeline.
Written once, linked from the payment page.
Bank, PayPal, or credit against a future trip. The third one costs us less and is worth more to them.

themes.name: Growth and recruiting
ideas: Rather than a form. Faster to judge, and it is the actual skill.
So opening Poland starts with fifty people rather than zero.
A public join page per market
In that market's language, even though the community stays English.
Chosen by the community rather than the team.
The people who left are the warmest source there is.
A place to park creators we have spotted but not approached, with who found them.
So an applicant knows where they are without emailing to ask.

themes.name: The platform itself
ideas: Messages, resources, creators, countries. Cmd+K searches commands, not content.
A message written in a tunnel should send when the signal returns.
"Three people here", not just online dots.
Keyboard paths through chat and the maps, focus order, contrast on the orange-on-orange states.
The initial bundle has crept back up; make a regression fail the build rather than be noticed six weeks later.
A staging environment with seeded data
Every UI bug in the last two sessions was found by hand on production data.
Click any admin statistic and see the query behind it. Analytics people trust get used.
One page showing every card, badge and button in both themes. Drift is invisible until you see them together.
The network preview is a localStorage flag. Rolling anything out to ten people needs a real switch.
Three redesigns of the same map pin in two sessions says the eye is the only test we have.
Rate limiting on the write paths
Nothing stops a script posting a thousand messages today.

themes.name: Games, now there are five
ideas: Challenge a specific creator to the same ten questions. The reason to open a game twice.
Built as a rounds game so it could be tested. Promote it.
Guess the city from a photo
From creators' own travel galleries, with their permission. The content already exists.
The UK against the Nordics, monthly. Markets need something to be about besides work.
The current bank is too easy for the well-travelled, which is everyone here.
A game a creator can set
Pick ten countries, name it, share the link. Admin-built games do not scale; creator-built ones do.
Hearing "kiitos" is the half of learning a phrase that reading it cannot do.

themes.name: Tryp.com itself
themes.note: The community only pays for itself if it feeds the business.
ideas: One route, one price, briefed. Gives the whole community something concrete to post about on the same day.
The best entries embedded on the destination pages they are about.
Marketing asks for a specific shot; creators claim it. Turns the community into a production line when it needs to be.
Booking data into the collab board
"Three creators are already flying to Lisbon that week" is more useful when it comes from real bookings.
What the programme actually returned, per market, per challenge. The number that decides next year's budget.
Written by the people who filmed there, published under tryp.com. SEO that only this community can produce.
